extraction.name: 94% on CIFAR-10 in 3.29 Seconds on a Single GPU
extraction.description: CIFAR-10 is among the most widely used datasets in machine learning, facilitating thousands of research projects per year. To accelerate research and reduce the cost of experiments, we introduce training methods for CIFAR-10 which reach 94% accuracy in 3.29 seconds, 95% in 10.4 seconds, and 96% in 46.3 seconds, when run on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU. As one factor contributing to these training speeds, we propose a derandomized variant of horizontal flipping augmentation, which we show improves over the standard method in every case where flipping is beneficial over no flipping at all.
extraction.creator: Keller Jordan
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The CIFAR-10 dataset contains 60,000 32x32 color images, each labeled as one of ten classes. It is divided into a training set of 50,000 images and a validation set of 10,000 images.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: For data augmentation, random horizontal flipping and 2-pixel random translation with reflection padding were used. A derandomized variant of horizontal flipping augmentation, called alternating flip, was proposed and used. For 96% accuracy, 12-pixel Cutout augmentation was added. During evaluation, horizontal flipping test-time augmentation (TTA) was used, where the network is run on both a given test image and its mirror. For multi-crop evaluation (tta_level=2), predictions were generated by running the trained network on six augmented views of each test image: the unmodified input, a version translated up-and-to-the-left by one pixel, a version translated down-and-to-the-right by one pixel, and the mirrored versions of all three. Predictions were made using a weighted average of all six outputs, where the two views of the untranslated image are weighted by 0.25 each, and the remaining four views are weighted by 0.125 each.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images were loaded as uint8, then converted to half-precision floating point, scaled by 1/255, and permuted to channels_last format. Images were normalized using CIFAR_MEAN (0.4914, 0.4822, 0.4465) and CIFAR_STD (0.2470, 0.2435, 0.2616). Images were pre-padded with reflection padding for random translation augmentation.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, and Validation of machine learning models for image classification tasks. The dataset is widely used in machine learning research to accelerate experiments and reduce computational costs.
